_note: Plain-English wording for the bundled puzzle's 74 deduction steps, written once and stored so the demo needs no API key and costs nothing. Regenerate with: python -m narrate_example --api-key sk-ant-... . The keys are group ids from to_ai_payload; every id must appear exactly once, which narrate.problems_with checks.

prose.1: "The green house is immediately to the right of the ivory house" needs a house on each side of the pair, so ivory can't be house 5 with nothing to its right, and green can't be house 1 with nothing to its left.
prose.2: "Milk is drunk in the middle house" pins milk to house 3. That rules milk out of every other house, and rules every other drink out of house 3.
prose.3: House 3 has nothing left to drink but milk, so milk it is.
prose.4: "The Norwegian lives in the first house" puts the Norwegian in house 1, which keeps him out of houses 2 to 5 and keeps everyone else out of house 1.
prose.5: House 1 has no other nationality left, so the Norwegian lives there.
prose.6: The Lucky Strike smoker drinks orange juice, but house 3 drinks milk, so house 3 isn't the Lucky Strike smoker.
prose.7: The Japanese smokes Parliaments, and house 1 is the Norwegian, so nobody in house 1 smokes Parliaments.
prose.8: The Englishman lives in the red house, and house 1 is the Norwegian, so house 1 isn't red.
prose.9: The Spaniard owns the dog, and house 1 is the Norwegian, so the dog isn't in house 1.
prose.10: Coffee is drunk in the green house, and house 1 can't be green, so house 1 doesn't drink coffee.
prose.11: Coffee is drunk in the green house, but house 3 drinks milk, so house 3 isn't green.
prose.12: The Ukrainian drinks tea, and house 3 drinks milk, so house 3 isn't the Ukrainian.
prose.13: The Ukrainian drinks tea, and house 1 is the Norwegian, so house 1 doesn't drink tea.
prose.14: Green sits immediately right of ivory, and green can no longer be house 3, so ivory can't be house 2.
prose.15: Whichever side of the Norwegian the blue house sits on, the same thing follows every time: house 1 can't be blue, and house 2 can't be red, green or yellow.
prose.16: Blue is the only colour house 2 has left, so house 2 is blue.
prose.17: Whichever side of the Norwegian the blue house sits on, it comes out at house 2 every time — so houses 3, 4 and 5 cannot be blue.
prose.18: The Englishman lives in the red house, and house 2 is blue, so house 2 isn't the Englishman.
prose.19: Coffee is drunk in the green house, and house 2 is blue, so house 2 doesn't drink coffee.
prose.20: Green sits immediately right of ivory, and house 2 is blue rather than green, so house 1 can't be ivory.
prose.21: House 1 is not red, green, ivory or blue, so the only colour left for it is yellow.
prose.22: Kools are smoked in the yellow house, and house 2 is blue, so house 2 doesn't smoke Kools.
prose.23: Both ways the Chesterfield smoker could sit next to the fox owner lead to the same place: yellow is out for houses 3, 4 and 5.
prose.24: Checking each way Kools could sit next to the horse rules the horse out of house 1.
prose.25: Kools are smoked in the yellow house, and house 3 can't be yellow, so house 3 doesn't smoke Kools.
prose.26: Kools are smoked in the yellow house, and house 4 can't be yellow, so house 4 doesn't smoke Kools.
prose.27: Kools are smoked in the yellow house, and house 5 can't be yellow, so house 5 doesn't smoke Kools.
prose.28: Working through both ways Chesterfields could neighbour the fox, house 1 comes out the same each time: not Old Gold, not Chesterfields, not Lucky Strike.
prose.29: With everything else ruled out for house 1, Kools is the only brand left there.
prose.30: Testing each way Kools could sit next to the horse leaves house 2 with no snails, no fox, no dog and no zebra.
prose.31: The horse is the only pet house 2 has left, so the horse lives there.
prose.32: Working through both ways round again, the horse settles at house 2, so houses 3, 4 and 5 do not have it.
prose.33: The Lucky Strike smoker drinks orange juice, and house 1 smokes Kools, so house 1 doesn't drink juice.
prose.34: House 1 has no coffee, no tea, no milk and no juice left, so it drinks water.
prose.35: Whichever side the blue house falls on, water ends up settled in house 1, so houses 2, 4 and 5 can't have it.
prose.36: The Spaniard owns the dog, and house 2 keeps the horse, so house 2 isn't the Spaniard.
prose.37: The Old Gold smoker owns snails, and house 2 keeps the horse, so house 2 doesn't smoke Old Gold.
prose.38: The Old Gold smoker owns snails, and house 1 smokes Kools, so house 1 doesn't own the snails.
prose.39: Putting the Japanese in house 2 broke the puzzle, so that is ruled out.
prose.40: House 2 is not English, Spanish, Norwegian or Japanese, so the Ukrainian lives there.
prose.41: Trying the Spaniard in house 3, and then the Japanese, each broke the puzzle.
prose.42: With the Spaniard, the Japanese, the Ukrainian and the Norwegian all ruled out of house 3, the Englishman lives there.
prose.43: Putting the Ukrainian, the Japanese or the Englishman in house 4 broke the puzzle each time.
prose.44: That leaves only the Spaniard for house 4.
prose.45: The Ukrainian, the Spaniard and the Englishman each broke the puzzle when tried in house 5.
prose.46: So house 5 is the Japanese, the only nationality left.
prose.47: Making house 3 ivory broke the puzzle.
prose.48: House 3 isn't green, ivory, yellow or blue, so it must be red.
prose.49: House 4 broke the puzzle as red, and broke it again as green.
prose.50: With yellow and blue already gone too, house 4 must be ivory.
prose.51: House 5 broke the puzzle when it was red.
prose.52: House 5 can't be ivory, yellow or blue either, so it is green.
prose.53: Giving house 1 the zebra broke the puzzle.
prose.54: No dog, no snails, no horse and no zebra leaves the fox for house 1.
prose.55: House 3 broke the puzzle with the dog, with the zebra, and with the fox.
prose.56: The horse is elsewhere, so the snails are what remain for house 3.
prose.57: The snails, the zebra and the fox each broke the puzzle in house 4.
prose.58: With the horse ruled out as well, house 4 keeps the dog.
prose.59: House 5 broke the puzzle with the snails, the dog and the fox.
prose.60: The horse is taken, so house 5 keeps the zebra.
prose.61: Giving house 2 the orange juice broke the puzzle.
prose.62: House 2 has no coffee, no milk, no water and no juice, so it drinks tea.
prose.63: House 4 broke the puzzle drinking coffee, and again drinking tea.
prose.64: Milk and water are already placed, so house 4 drinks the orange juice.
prose.65: House 5 broke the puzzle with juice and with tea.
prose.66: Milk and water are gone too, so house 5 drinks the coffee.
prose.67: Parliaments in house 2 broke the puzzle, and so did Lucky Strike.
prose.68: Old Gold and Kools were already out, so house 2 smokes Chesterfields.
prose.69: House 3 broke the puzzle smoking Parliaments, and again smoking Chesterfields.
prose.70: Kools and Lucky Strike are ruled out too, so house 3 smokes Old Gold.
prose.71: Parliaments, Chesterfields and Old Gold each broke the puzzle in house 4.
prose.72: With Kools gone as well, house 4 smokes Lucky Strike.
prose.73: House 5 broke the puzzle with Chesterfields, Lucky Strike and Old Gold.
prose.74: Kools is taken by house 1, so house 5 smokes Parliaments — and that finishes the grid.
